axes.brief:
Hereditary rulers and their Federal Supreme Council choose national government; limited advisory elections do not make national leadership electorally accountable.
Focused six-question reassessment: Hereditary rulers appoint national governing and advisory bodies, with technical administration under political authority. There is no competitive public national electoral mandate to postpone; the statutory election claim is a mixed analogy, not a claim about actual universal elections.
axes.counterEvidence:
Collective ruler decision-making, FNC scrutiny and formal constitutional jurisdiction qualify claims of unlimited personal power; advisory elections are not competitive government selection.
The owner-defined broader axis includes lawful delegation and direct public control; a lower numerical placement is not a regime classification. Six exact responses and response strengths remain inferred. Retained source access dates are not refreshed unless a source was actually revisited. Unchanged answers and other axes were not re-audited. Hereditary rulers appoint national governing and advisory bodies, with technical administration under political authority. There is no competitive public national electoral mandate to postpone; the statutory election claim is a mixed analogy, not a claim about actual universal elections.

Focused interpretation: Hereditary rulers appoint national governing and advisory bodies, with technical administration under political authority. This is delegation of policy decisions to independent specialists, not replacement of the electorate or a claim that all expertise is political sovereignty. A legislative mandate, appointment process and later review can coexist with not voting on every operational decision.
